newsitem.title: UK: Daimler says hedging hits financial result.
newsitem.headline: Daimler says hedging hits financial result.

text.p: Germany's Daimler-Benz AG said on Thursday that although it had benefited strongly from the effects of the strong dollar on its sales of cars and aircraft, its currency hedging had hit its financial results.

The company told its half-year results news conference in London that the financial result in its profit and loss account had swung to a loss of 111 million marks in the January to June period from a profit of 205 million in the same year earlier period.
"Most of that change is due to hedging. We hedged a lot at around 1.60 DM and now the dollar is at 1.84 so we have to account for the difference," a spokesman told Reuters.

The company said in its interim report: "These corrections are performed not for losses actually incurred but only for profits not realised. They are offset by corresponding value increases in the underlying transactions."
The company also said that while it had a tax credit of 200 million marks in 1996 due to the development of deferred taxes, it had a tax expense of 300 million in the first half of 1997.
"The consolidated net income thus reached 1.0 billion marks which is 0.2 billion higher than the corresponding period in the previous year," Daimler added.
